title: Practicing in the cellar studio in Vienna
summary: Practice routine and privacy in Vienna versus New York, and living in the 18th district.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you still have a daily routine? Do you still practice daily?

Yeah, sure, I still practice. That’s one thing that keeps me in Vienna since my wife died was that I can practice over there like I can’t practice here because the house that we have… [has] a studio down in the cellar, so I don’t have to worry about bothering anybody. I find that a very inhibiting thing that if you’re gonna try to practice with the idea in your mind that you’re dragging somebody else. But, if you have privacy, then you can do whatever you want to do when you want to do it. When I’m here in New York, the place that I live [in] I can’t practice there because somebody next door is a psychiatrist.
You can practice there now because they’re just messing it up [referring to construction] [laughs].

Oh yeah, the last couple days [laughs]. So, what I have to do [is] I have to go over to a studio, which I can do. I have a key to a studio. I can get over there anytime I want to. I’m spoiled now because I’m used to taking the stairs down to the cellar.
You live in what they call the 18th District?
Yeah, very quiet. Good air, that’s it.
